note: Every page that exists on more than one archive, and whether it has been given a shared shape. `state` is aligned, partial or local. This is what the cross-archive work list is counted against: a route that is not aligned is outstanding work, and a work-list row has to say which routes it answers for. Tier is the order I mean to do them in, not a claim about importance.

rows.note: Metrics, timeline, ranked chart, couples, families — one component, one order.
The five-word evidence ladder, shared since before this session.
One component, and now two gates behind it.
Shared.
Shared Atlas on all six that have it.
All seven on the shared chart.

**Five of seven on the shared FilterTable** — Falco, Defranceschi, Booyzen, Blazevic, Mazza — each keeping its own columns, facets and prose. Falco went 378 lines to 280, Blazevic 182 to 80, Booyzen 141 to 57. **Nothing was surrendered to standardise**: the Blazevic spelling fold is a prop now (joannis still finds 118 Ivans), Falco's five booleans are still one row of mutually exclusive buttons, and the links gained trailing slashes — 9,750 redirects removed on the Falco page alone. **D'Arcy and Lerena do not have a table here at all** and need reading before they are moved.

**Five of seven on the shared EveryName.** Three were byte-identical apart from the import line; Falco and Booyzen differed only in wording. **The other two are a different page under the same label**: Defranceschi's /who/ is a PERSON index grouped by letter and D'Arcy's is the people it met in documents and had nowhere to put — witnesses, constables, surgeons. That is for you to settle, not for a component to paper over.

**Two of seven on the shared Register** — Falco (12,034 records) and Blazevic (1,466), which were near-identical forks. **Size is legitimate and stays**: an archive that has read more registers has more records, and equalising them would mean deleting evidence. The SHAPE is what is shared. The per-surname sections became a facet. **The Falco page is also 1.9 MB smaller than the one deployed** — both pages duplicated every row's text into an attribute for the search to read; the script reads the row instead. **Defranceschi, Booyzen and D'Arcy hold a register in a different shape** (id/says/place, positional arrays, grouped by surname) and need reading before they move. Mazza and Lerena have none.

**Four of seven on the shared Searched** — Defranceschi, D'Arcy, Blazevic, Mazza, 835 searches between them. One model, four spellings. **The outcome words stay the archive's**: hit/yield/nothing/found/pending, yield/null/empty/blocked, +partly, done/outstanding/not-yet/superseded — those are different judgements about what a search DID, not synonyms. Tags survived, which needed a multi-value facet (a row carries several and a reader clicks one). D'Arcy keeps the thing no one else records: whether a null had a control that could have disproved it. **Falco and Lerena have no searched.json** — Falco's page is prose, which is also why its work list could not be counted.

**Five of seven on the shared Corrections** — Falco, Defranceschi, Booyzen, Blazevic, Lerena — each keeping its own page title and its own words. **Not a table**: the first attempt put «what was said» and «what is true» in four columns and it was unreadable, because these are sentences. The shape promoted is Falco's, already the best of the seven. **What a correction is filtered by stays local**: Booyzen grades by CAUSE (a list mistaken for a population, a search written up as wider than it was), Falco and Defranceschi by severity, Blazevic not at all. **Mazza has none recorded yet and D'Arcy writes them inline in the page** — those two need reading, not converting.

**Two of seven, and that is the ceiling until the others extract their questions.** Only Defranceschi (q/status/known/needed) and D'Arcy (q/state/rank/settles/tried) hold questions as DATA; **Falco, Booyzen, Blazevic, Lerena and Mazza write them as prose**, so they cannot adopt this until somebody turns them into rows — research work belonging to each archive, not something to guess from outside. The shape is: the question, what is known, what has been tried, and **the specific record that would answer it**. That last field is what makes it a queue rather than a list of regrets. D'Arcy also ages a question and marks anything past thirty days.

All seven on the shared Spine, and the point of it is the mark on the joint that cannot bear weight. Four archives had that argument in prose beside a row that said nothing: Booyzen's seventh generation, Mazza's four unsourced, Defranceschi's first. Lerena's chain is deliberately unmarked and that now means something. The spine carries a household, a Latin form, a trade, sources and an archive's own plate renderer, so Defranceschi lost nothing moving onto it.

All seven on the shared register. A kind - farm, village, church, hospital, cemetery - is now its own column and filter, because a cemetery holding four people is not the evidence a farm holding four is. Four archives keep a second, local table beside it (Falco's record locations, Blazevic's how-far-wrong, Mazza's export-vs-map spellings) and those stay.
**503 to 11,809 words.** What each archive rests on.

Five of seven draw 'where the name is' on the shared Distribution (Falco, Lerena, Booyzen, D'Arcy, Defranceschi via its own spelling wrapper). TWO ARE NOT A GAP TO CLOSE BY FORCE. Blazevic's four-row table compares the rarity of four SURNAMES, not the geography of one, and carries a principal-countries column the chart cannot hold. Mazza holds no worldwide distribution data at all - only how many of each name this archive itself holds - and inventing a chart for it would be research, not alignment. Where a chart would contradict its own page it is drawn differently: Lerena ranks by density because that page argues Spain is not the answer.

All seven on the shared chronology. The chart above it stays each archive's - sovereignty lanes, political bands and Falco's read-coverage band each say something the others cannot - but the dated events, their grouping, their filter and the source beside each row are now one shape.

All six that keep one are on the shared feed. Mazza has no such page. Booyzen sets withdrawals beside findings on the day they happened and that arrangement was kept for all six; the strikethrough table stays on /corrections/.

Four of five on the shared Households. Three things came out of the four and now belong to all of them: Booyzen's record of HOW each household and each child is known, D'Arcy's search box, and Defranceschi's mark on a child who did not reach five - which the warning at the foot of every one of these pages had been making an excuse about. FALCO IS THE EXCEPTION AND SHOULD STAY ONE: its page is an evidence register grouped by household - person, event, date, what the register says, ark - not a list of couples with children under them, and the shared card would flatten four columns into a name chip.
Four archives; two of them call it something else on the page.
Three archives.
Three archives, and two are about different subjects — this one may stay local.
